subject: Tailored fleet fit & response-length probe for CrowdEdge pilot
messages:
From: Evan Cole <evan@crowdedge.ai>
To: maya_srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-11T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity inquiry: CrowdEdge pilot

Hi Maya,

Thanks for taking this — CrowdEdge is considering a small dedicated deployment to run our chat + summarization pilot. High level: we expect roughly 120 sustained QPS during business hours with spikes to ~280 QPS for short bursts (20-30 minutes). Primary model is a 13B-ish open family (we're flexible).

To help your sizing team, here's what we have on hand:
- Peak concurrent sessions (websocket-style session affinity): ~300
- Avg prompt length: 45 tokens (typical customer query + context)
- Avg response length: 220 tokens; median ~110 but long-tail up to 2.5k tokens for batch summaries
- Session retention: most sessions are <90s but ~8% are long-running (10–15 minutes) with iterative turns
- SLA target: p95 generation latency <= 350ms for interactive flows
- We will use prefix caching for common system prompts if supported

Can you share the questionnaire or traffic schema you prefer (prompt/response histograms, dayparting, burst windows) so we can attach the actual logs? Also: are there recommended GPU SKUs you typically propose for this profile and what guardrails should we expect for burst capacity?

I'll attach a small sample of telemetry in a follow-up note — Jose (infra lead) is copied.

Best,
Evan
CTO, CrowdEdge

Hi Evan — great to meet you. Thanks for the summary; that profile is in the range we see for interactive note/summarization products. Attached is a short intake template we use to normalize sizing data. If you can fill the highlighted sections it will speed up our sizing pass. Quick asks below as well.

Required fields (short form):
1) Traffic by hour (sample CSV) — please include timestamp, qps, concurrent_sessions, avg_prompt_tokens, avg_response_tokens.
2) Prompt/response length distribution (percentiles: p50/p90/p99 and tail bucket >1024 tokens).
3) Session behavior: average turns per session, fraction of long-running sessions (>5min).
4) Model family and if you plan to use quantized variants (8-bit/4-bit) or opt for FP16.
5) Acceptable fallback plan: degrade to smaller model or increase latency during bursts?
6) Any regulatory constraints (data residency, KMS/HSM).

Attachments we can accept: CSVs, sample prompts (txt), histogram images. We'll attach an internal checklist and ask the sizing team to respond within 48 hours of receiving the filled template.

Two immediate notes: (a) given your p95 target and the long-tail responses, prefix/KV cache will help reduce token work on repeated system prompts; (b) bursts of ~280 QPS with 2.5k token tail responses will push memory-bound GPUs — we'll likely recommend a mixed SKU approach.

If you can send the template back today/tomorrow, I'll loop in our sizing engineers for a quick look.

Best,
Maya Srinivasan
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity inquiry: CrowdEdge pilot — sizing inputs attached

Maya / Karthik — quick sizing recommendation for CrowdEdge pilot (concise):

1) Proposed pilot fleet (3-month):
- 6 x H100 (80GB) nodes dedicated as primary serving pool: good for long-tail large responses and lower p95 under FP16.
- 2 x A100 (40GB) nodes as burst/overflow pool (auto-failover): cost-effective for medium-length responses and can accept quantized variants.
- Rationale: H100s reduce kernel fragmentation for >1k-token responses; A100s give cheaper density for steady 120 QPS.

2) Memory and session guidance:
- Expect ~30–45 interactive sessions per H100 for configs with 220–400 token average responses with FP16. Long responses (2k tokens) reduce concurrency by ~40% per-GPU due to KV cache and attention state.
- Recommend enabling prefix/KV caching for repeated system prompts — reduces work by ~15–30% depending on repetition.

3) Burst handling & fallback policy:
- Use Dedicated + reserved burst pool: primary H100 pool handles baseline; during burst allocate sessions to A100 pool; enable automatic fallback to a smaller model only for non-critical flows (we can implement transparent model cascade so the UI falls back to a summarized variant, not raw degraded output).
- For strict p95 interactive flows, prefer increasing latency slightly over switching to a different semantic model — this avoids quality regressions.

4) Cost & ops notes (order-of-magnitude for 3 months):
- H100s (6): estimate list compute + infra $~150k–$220k/month (depending on region and redundancy).
- A100s (2): additional $~20k–$35k/month.
- Add-ons: Dedicated SLA + 24/7 on-call and longer log retention are incremental.

5) Next steps to finalize quote:
- Get a full 7-day CSV (we can run a sanity ingest to simulate token cost).
- Confirm model binary (FP16 image path) and planned quantization timeline.
- Book a 30-min sizing call with CrowdEdge + infra to walk through edge cases (long batch summaries).

I'll draft a short proposal we can send to Evan with the SKU mix, fallback options, and a ballpark cost range once we ingest the CSV.

—Marissa
Solutions Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
